label: Plausible capacity factor for a home GPU inference node (% of hours serving paid work)
value_text: ~5-35% of wall-clock hours; ~15% central estimate for a single residential node
source_name: Synthesized bound from Akash (~50-70% network-wide, datacenter-grade), io.net (~2% active), Salad/Render idle-only models, Vast.ai (80% marketing best-case vs idle-consumer reality)
notes: DERIVED bound, not a single published figure - flagged low confidence. Reasoning: (1) Even the best-run decentralized DATACENTER network (Akash) tops out ~50-70% and that is an aggregate over pooled, reliable capacity - a ceiling, not a home-node baseline. (2) Consumer/home-hardware networks (io.net ~2% active, Salad/Render explicitly idle-only) realize far less paid time per node because of reliability filtering, buyer preference for verified hosts, residential downtime (gaming, sleep, power/network drops), and dynamic-NAT reachability. (3) Vast.ai's own 80% is an explicit best-case marketing assumption for a well-run verified rig, and its guidance says below ~60% renting beats owning. (4) Demand is bursty and concentrates on trusted/high-density hosts, so a new single residential node captures little. A due-diligence revenue model should use ~10-20% as the base case, stress-test down to ~5%, and treat >35% as optimistic requiring reserved/committed contracts and verified-host reliability. Note this is the DUTY-CYCLE (hours serving), distinct from within-request SM utilization (~19-40%) which further discounts effective throughput/energy-billing.
verdict_note: This is a synthesized bound, not a single sourced figure, and is appropriately marked low-confidence. The ~5-35% wall-clock paid-serving band with a ~15% central estimate for a single residential node is well-reasoned and consistent with the underlying evidence once each input is read correctly: io.net ~2% active (extreme low), Render/Salad idle-only with no published duty cycle and inflated 'availability' rewards, Vast.ai ~40-60% real (verified best-case) vs 80% marketing, and Akash's ~50% being datacenter-grade fleet leasing not a home duty cycle. A single home node lacking sustained concurrency and 24/7 verified availability plausibly sits in the low-to-mid teens percent. Range retained.
